episodes.169439: With an abundant amount of moisture across northern and central New Mexico, the Fourth of July holiday was a busy one across the area. Numerous thunderstorms impacted the area, some of which produced locally heavy rainfall. Thunderstorms near Mexican Springs in McKinley County caused flash flooding along area roadways during the evening hours.
episodes.169443: With the area of high pressure still centered to the east of New Mexico, southerly flow across the area continued to allow for subtropical moisture to stream into the area. Meanwhile, some drier air working into western New Mexico began to have a noticeable impact on storm coverage and intensity. Despite this, thunderstorms were still capable of producing locally heavy rain, and one thunderstorm near Nageezi south of Farmington caused flash flooding along U.S. Highway 550.
episodes.169530: Very hot temperatures on the afternoon of the fourth allowed for isolated thunderstorms to develop on the South Plains. episodes.169531: A third consecutive afternoon of very hot temperatures allowed isolated thunderstorms to develop across the region under a monsoonal fetch of mid-level moisture. A relatively dry sub-cloud layer allowed a couple of these storms to produce severe downburst winds in Lubbock (Lubbock County) and near Turkey (Hall County).
episodes.169598: Ample monsoon moisture paired with the aided support aloft from a passing shortwave resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across western Colorado. Some storms produced heavy rain which led to a localized debris flow in Mesa County.
episodes.169608: Four separate rounds of thunderstorms impacted central and northern portions of Rush County through the afternoon and early evening of July 5th, with tree damage noted during the second round.  A couple of trees that were downed or damaged near Carthage and the northside of Rushville had been weakened by severe storms on July 1st.  Later in the evening, an isolated storm caused widespread minor tree damage to Muncie.

episodes.169877: A line of strong to severe storms moved south along the Lake Michigan shoreline late in the evening on July 4, 2022.

These storms brought strong, gusty winds, severe hail, moderate to heavy rainfall, and lightning, causing notable damage to property, specifically crops.
episodes.170053: Disturbances moved through a persistent southwest flow aloft across the region, which continued to provide daily afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms. These storms, some of which were severe, brought strong, gusty winds, severe hail, heavy localized rainfall, and lightning.
episodes.170237: A few strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of the Nebraska Panhandle late in the afternoon on the 4th with strong winds and hail.
episodes.170503: Scattered showers and thunderstorms moved southeast across the mid Ohio Valley as an upper level disturbance pushed through the mid Ohio Valley.

episodes.170584: A derecho swept across South Dakota and into Iowa on the evening of July 5th. This resulted in a swath of  wind gust from 50 to 65 plus mph resulting in a number of power outages, tree damage, and a few damaged structures. A brief tornado occurred near Estherville with minor damage. As the bowing thunderstorm complex reach central Iowa the gusts had dropped below severe criteria given the less favorable environment with decreased deep layer shear.
episodes.170603: A few thunderstorms, including an isolated supercell, produced sporadic wind damage and a couple of tornadoes along a stalled warm front.

episodes.170825: A thunderstorm became severe over southeastern Crook County, producing large hail east of Sundance.

episodes.170914: A couple of isolated severe thunderstorms containing large hail and very heavy rain occurred during the late evening of the 4th and early morning hours of the 5th.
episodes.171046: A stationary front draped north of West Viginia led to several rounds of showers and storms between July 5th and 6th. Overnight clusters of activity diminished each morning, allowing for a brief window of reprieve. This allowed the atmosphere to recharge for renewed convection during the afternoon and evening time frame. These storms contributed to downed trees from damaging wind gusts and localized instances of flash flooding due to heavy downpours. Over an inch of rain fell within strong and mature storms on these two days.
episodes.171089: Storms developed along a frontal boundary in far northeast Nebraska leading to several severe wind reports across a few counties.
episodes.171094: Storms developed along a frontal boundary in far northeast Nebraska leading to several severe wind reports across a few counties.
episodes.171099: A complex of storms moved eastward across Chesapeake Bay and into Delmarva. The storms produced some wind damage and two brief tornadoes on the western shore of Maryland, but weakened into the eastern shore. However, one isolated case of tree damage was reported near Harrington as the storms moved into Delaware.
episodes.171252: An early morning supercell thunderstorm tracked across northern Harding County and expanded into a line of severe storms across Perkins into Ziebach and Haakon Counties. The storms primarily produced large hail initially, then strong wind gusts and hail accompanied the storms as they moved toward central South Dakota.
episodes.171257: An early morning thunderstorm became severe as it passed over northeastern Perkins County. The storm produced hail around golf ball size.
episodes.171259: A line of severe thunderstorms developed across northwestern South Dakota during the morning and tracked east-southeast into west central South Dakota before weakening. The storms produced wind gusts to 70 mph across portions of the area.
episodes.171260: A thunderstorm became severe over Todd County, producing wind gusts around 60 mph.
episodes.171261: A severe thunderstorm clipped northern and eastern portions of Tripp County as it moved southeast across the region, producing wind gusts over 60 mph.
episodes.171270: Strong to severe thunderstorms erupted along a slow moving cold front over southern WI. Large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding occurred. A lightning strike and subsequent fire caused significant damage to a home in Beloit.
episodes.171506: An outflow boundary from severe storms in South Dakota raced southward into Nebraska during the afternoon of July 5, resulting in damaging winds in the northern Sandhills. Additional thunderstorms developed in far north central Nebraska and produced severe winds.
episodes.171612: Isolated supercell thunderstorms tracked from Converse and Niobrara counties into northern portions of Platte and Goshen counties during the mid to late afternoon hours on July 5th. These storms produced hail larger than 2 inches in diameter and wind gusts in excess of 70 MPH.
episodes.171613: A significant supercell produced very large and destructive hail larger than 4 inches in diameter across Sioux County during the late afternoon into the early evening hours on July 5th. Further south, another cluster of severe thunderstorms produced wind gusts in excess of 70 MPH near Sidney.
episodes.171665: Conditions became supportive of the development of waterspouts along the southeast South Carolina coast in the morning hours. A couple of waterspouts were reported just off the coast and developed along the morning land breeze.
episodes.171897: An upper level ridge was centered north and west of the region. That put the local area on the outer periphery of the ridge. Atmospheric moisture levels were very high, with a precipitable water value of 2.4 inches. That value is right at the average highest for this time of year. An easterly wave passing across the local area on the 5th provided the focus for convective development and was able to capitalize on the abundant moisture in place. One of the storms that developed was able to produce heavy rainfall resulting in flash flooding across New Orleans.
episodes.171918: Scattered storms moved across portions of northeast Iowa during the evening of July 4th. A few of these storms became strong enough to produce some hail across Fayette and Clayton Counties. The largest reported hail was quarter sized in Littleport (Clayton County) and Elkport (Clayton County).
episodes.171925: A line of storms moved across southwest Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening of July 5th. Some of these storms produced hail, with the largest reported being penny sized in Preston (Grant County).
episodes.171942: Thunderstorms developed over southeast Montana during the very early morning hours as a low level jet increased ahead of a series of weak short-wave troughs. The thunderstorms then moved into southwest North Dakota. One severe thunderstorm produced ping pong ball size hail near Bowman in Bowman County.
episodes.171983: On July 4th, evening thunderstorms developed in the far-southwestern portion of Nebraska. These thunderstorms produced microburst wind gusts that measured up to 84 mph.
episodes.172198: Severe thunderstorms developed in Montana during the evening of July 4th then moved into northwestern South Dakota during the early morning hours of July 5th. The storms intensified around daybreak on July 5th, as they encountered a more favorable environment for severe storms. The storms started as supercells and then evolved into a derecho, with embedded supercells as they moved through Hand and Hyde counties. The significant severe storms tracked southeast across central South Dakota, into southeastern South Dakota, and eventually into northern Iowa while producing winds up to 91 mph and hail to the size of softballs in central South Dakota. The storms caused widespread damage to trees, grain bins, crops, and vehicles. Some of the highest wind gusts include 91 mph 4 miles north of Agar, 87 mph 1 mile north of Ree Heights, 84 mph 1 mile south-southwest of Timber Lake, and 77 mph 12 miles east-southeast of Sunshine Bible Academy. Hail, 4 inches in diameter, was reported in Promise and 2 miles north of Timber Lake.
episodes.172262: A moist and destabilizing airmass existed ahead of an upper level storm system traveling across the periphery of a sprawling mid-summer ridge across the southern plains into the southeast U.S. This triggered multiple severe thunderstorms due to the modest shear and instability in place. One of these storms spawned a tornado in Grayson county.
episodes.172263: A moist and destabilizing airmass existed ahead of an upper level storm system traveling across the periphery of a sprawling mid-summer ridge across the southern plains into the southeast U.S. This triggered a few severe thunderstorms due to the modest shear and instability in place.
episodes.172381: A weak disturbance moving northward through central Arizona interacted with monsoon moisture already in place to initiate showers and thunderstorms across the area. The timing of peak heating and the arrival of the disturbance created heavy rain in the Page, Arizona area.
episodes.172476: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a warm front produced damaging winds and a tornado across portions of the Virginia Northern Neck.
episodes.172478: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a warm front produced a waterspout across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.172544: A complex of thunderstorms moved southeast from Kentucky and moved across southwest Virginia and East Tennessee. The storms produced hail and wind damage across portions of the area during the late afternoon and evening.
episodes.172630: A warm front draped from the Great Lakes into the Ohio Valley led to morning showers and thunderstorms across the Ohio Valley early in the day. These showers and storms continued to progress southward toward central North Carolina in the evening hours, especially across the northwest, central, and southern Piedmont. The storms did not completely clear the area until the early overnight hours, as storms by then moved into South Carolina. There were numerous reports of trees and power lines down across Guilford, Forsyth, and Davidson Counties, as well as wind damage reports over Granville, Person, and Franklin Counties. Isolated flash flooding also occurred in parts of Forsyth County.
episodes.172643: Three to seven inches of rain fell in Whitley and Allen Counties, IN on the morning of July 5. There was some tree damage in the area as these thunderstorms moved through.
episodes.172644: Kentucky was experiencing warm and moist SW flow heading through the day on July 5, while flow in the mid and upper levels was more westerly. While no forcing mechanism was in place across the state )as far as low pressure center, shortwave, or frontal boundary) and the better severe weather concerns were concentrated well to our NW, the low level wind sheer and decent Cape values were enough to create good boyancy and spawn showers and thunderstorms throughout the afternoon and evening. The main concern with these storms was strong winds being transferred down to the surface, which did result in multiple instances of downed trees. Heavy rain that impacted Clay County and Montgomery County also lead to a swift water rescue and isolated instances of flash flooding.
episodes.172675: Isolated thunderstorms moved northeast across Pinal County during the afternoon. One storm damaged the Apache Sky Casino near Dudleyville.
episodes.172747: A cluster of thunderstorms developed across eastern Montana and the western Dakotas during the morning hours. These storms organized and turned southeastward, feeding on rich inflow of post-frontal air with up to 3000 J/kg of MLCAPE and over 1000 J/kg of DCAPE. Along with strong storm-relative shear, parameters favored development of a strong cold pool and balanced mesocyclone, which spread southeast with the cluster and developed a strong and long-duration severe wind event which traversed South Dakota, southwest Minnesota, extreme northeast Nebraska, and northwest Iowa during the afternoon and early evening. The storm was classified as a derecho, and featured numerous wind gusts from 70 to 100 mph and considerable damage to trees, crops, powerlines, and structures along its path. In some cases, severe wind gusts persisted for more than 30 minutes.
episodes.172766: A line of thunderstorms moved southeast across western North Carolina during the evening. Several of the embedded storms produced locally damaging wind gusts.
episodes.172771: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed and moved over upstate South Carolina during the evening. A couple of the storms produced locally damaging wind gusts.
episodes.172894: Two bands of heavy rain impacted Okanogan county during the afternoon. Areas impacted included Northeast of Mazama and Conconully. Rainfall ranged from 0.5 to 0.9 for Mazama and 0.6 to 1.4 for Conconully. The burn scars of Cedar Creek and Muckamuck from 2021 were in the flood areas.

A supercell thunderstorm spawned a brief EF1 tornado just north of Bowie, MD in Prince Georges County late on Tuesday afternoon July 5th, 2022, between 5:31 and 5:34 PM EDT. This supercell spawned along the Howard/Montgomery County line as a result of a remnant mesoscale convective vortex moving through the region which had moved through the Ohio Valley earlier in the day. It evolved into a cluster of cells initially before splitting off into an individual supercell that would develop rotation as it moved out of southeastern Montgomery County into northwestern Prince Georges County. The tornado caused extensive tree damage in the Somerset subdivision just north of Bowie, MD. There was also one instance where a tree had fallen on top of a residence near the intersection of Stafford Lane near Saber Lane. However, there were several other trees down in the area outside of the more concentrated tornadic damage, particularly along Buckingham Drive perpendicular to White Marsh Branch. At this location along Buckingham Drive, trees fell upon power lines, snapping several supporting utility poles. The tornado initially touched down around Tarragon Lane and tracked eastward over the Bowie High School Annex before tracking into the Somerset subdivision, where the majority of the damage was observed. The tornado would then lift just before reaching southern portions of Whitemarsh Park.

A supercell thunderstorm spawned a brief tornado just north of Harwood, Maryland (4 miles southwest of Londontowne) in Anne Arundel County late Tuesday afternoon July 5th, 2022, between 5:55 and 5:56 PM EDT. This supercell originally developed along the Howard/Montgomery County line as a result of a remnant mesoscale convective vortex (MCV) moving through the region which had moved through the Ohio Valley earlier in the day. It evolved into a cluster of cells initially before splitting off into an individual supercell that would develop rotation as it moved out of southeastern Montgomery County into northwestern Prince Georges County. The cell dropped a tornado earlier in the afternoon near Bowie, and would then cycle to produce the second tornado in Harwood. A broadcast media partner provided video and eyewitness evidence of a brief spin-up tornado while located at the intersection of Birdsville Road and MD-2 Solomons Island Road. This individual noted that the tornado was located just to their north in an open field and was on the ground for about one minute.
